answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by making reputation expensive to build and impossible to copy. Each identity earns trust only through a verifiable history of completed work tied to a persistent keypair: credibility accrues slowly, like a reef built grain by grain, while a brand-new identity stands on a bare ledge with strict rate limits and escrow on every deal. A Sybil attacker must therefore pay the full cost of real work for each fake identity, and any misbehavior burns that investment, since an ivory record of honest work cannot be forged overnight.
